answer: An operator rotating funds across many keys as a result bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never burns. Because the relic fee is applied at the willow exit, the spiral audit totals the burn and the ledger exposes exactly what left. Withdrawing stake burns a 5% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. That is 16 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
